literal: With me, it is as with you.'
idiomatic: With me, it is as with you.'

literal: Your ancestor thereupon memorialized thanks, thinking to move the state here; for more than ten generations army and people have all been attached to the soil and heavy to move, and could not return.
idiomatic: Your ancestor thereupon memorialized thanks, thinking to move the state here; for more than ten generations army and people have all been attached to the soil and heavy to move, and could not return.

literal: Thus with your state it is not a single day's goodwill.
idiomatic: Thus with your state it is not a single day's goodwill.

literal: Now I shall go west to the Great Food; I borrow passage through your state — do not give rise to suspicion."
idiomatic: Now I shall go west to the Great Food; I borrow passage through your state — do not give rise to suspicion."

literal: Bilgege received the letter and at once welcomed him to the lodge and feasted him three days.
idiomatic: Bilgege received the letter and at once welcomed him to the lodge and feasted him three days.

literal: On departure he presented six hundred horses, one hundred camels, and three thousand sheep, wished to pledge sons and grandsons as vassals, and escorted him to the border.
idiomatic: On departure he presented six hundred horses, one hundred camels, and three thousand sheep, wished to pledge sons and grandsons as vassals, and escorted him to the border.

literal: Where he passed, those who opposed he overcame; those who submitted he pacified.
idiomatic: Where he passed, those who opposed he overcame; those who submitted he pacified.

literal: The army marched ten thousand li; states that returned numbered several; camels, horses, cattle, sheep, and goods obtained could not be counted.
idiomatic: The army marched ten thousand li; states that returned numbered several; camels, horses, cattle, sheep, and goods obtained could not be counted.

literal: Army power daily grew; keen spirit daily doubled.
idiomatic: Army power daily grew; keen spirit daily doubled.

literal: Reaching Xunsi Gan, the various states of the Western Regions gathered troops of one hundred thousand, styled Qusun, and came to resist battle.
idiomatic: Reaching Xunsi Gan, the various states of the Western Regions gathered troops of one hundred thousand, styled Qusun, and came to resist battle.

literal: The two armies faced each other about two li.
idiomatic: The two armies faced each other about two li.

literal: He addressed the officers and soldiers, saying, "Though their army is many it is without plan; if we attack, head and tail will not rescue each other — our army is sure to win.
idiomatic: He addressed the officers and soldiers, saying, "Though their army is many it is without plan; if we attack, head and tail will not rescue each other — our army is sure to win.

literal: " He sent Six Courts Office great king Xiao Wolila, commissioner for suppression deputy Yelü Songshan, and others to lead two thousand five hundred troops attacking their right;
idiomatic: " He sent Six Courts Office great king Xiao Wolila, commissioner for suppression deputy Yelü Songshan, and others to lead two thousand five hundred troops attacking their right;

literal: privy deputy Xiao Chala Abu, [8] commissioner for suppression Yelü Shuxue, and others to lead two thousand five hundred troops attacking their left;
idiomatic: privy deputy Xiao Chala Abu, [8] commissioner for suppression Yelü Shuxue, and others to lead two thousand five hundred troops attacking their left;

literal: he himself with the mass attacked the center.
idiomatic: he himself with the mass attacked the center.

literal: The three armies all advanced; Qusun was greatly defeated; corpses lay for several tens of li.
idiomatic: The three armies all advanced; Qusun was greatly defeated; corpses lay for several tens of li.

literal: Encamped at Xunsi Gan altogether ninety days; the Huihui king came to submit and presented local products.
idiomatic: Encamped at Xunsi Gan altogether ninety days; the Huihui king came to submit and presented local products.

literal: Again going west to Qier Man, civil and military hundred officials invested Dashi as emperor; on jiachen year second month fifth day he took the throne, age thirty-eight, styled Gur Khan.
idiomatic: Again going west to Qier Man, civil and military hundred officials invested Dashi as emperor; on jiachen year second month fifth day he took the throne, age thirty-eight, styled Gur Khan.

literal: Again he took the Han honorific title Heavenly Emperor and changed the era to Yanqing.
idiomatic: Again he took the Han honorific title Heavenly Emperor and changed the era to Yanqing.

literal: He posthumously titled his grandfather Heir of the Source Emperor and his grandmother Virtuous Consort Empress; he invested primary consort Lady Xiao as Bright Virtue Empress.
idiomatic: He posthumously titled his grandfather Heir of the Source Emperor and his grandmother Virtuous Consort Empress; he invested primary consort Lady Xiao as Bright Virtue Empress.

literal: He thereupon said to the hundred officials, "I with you have marched thirty thousand li, toiled through desert, day and night in hardship.
idiomatic: He thereupon said to the hundred officials, "I with you have marched thirty thousand li, toiled through desert, day and night in hardship.

literal: Relying on the ancestors' blessing and your strength, we have rashly ascended the great position.
idiomatic: Relying on the ancestors' blessing and your strength, we have rashly ascended the great position.

literal: Your ancestors and fathers should receive added favor; together enjoy honor and glory.
idiomatic: Your ancestors and fathers should receive added favor; together enjoy honor and glory.

literal: " From Xiao Wolila and forty-nine others' grandfathers, titles were granted in differing degrees.
idiomatic: " From Xiao Wolila and forty-nine others' grandfathers, titles were granted in differing degrees.

literal: Son Yilie
idiomatic: Son Yilie

literal: Son Yilie was young; testamentary order had the empress hold state.
idiomatic: Son Yilie was young; testamentary order had the empress hold state.

literal: Later name Tabuyan, title Gantian Empress; she held rule, changed the era to Xianqing, on the throne seven years.
idiomatic: Later name Tabuyan, title Gantian Empress; she held rule, changed the era to Xianqing, on the throne seven years.

literal: Son Yilie took the throne and changed the era to Shaoxing.
idiomatic: Son Yilie took the throne and changed the era to Shaoxing.

literal: Registering the people eighteen sui and above, he obtained eighty-four thousand five hundred households.
idiomatic: Registering the people eighteen sui and above, he obtained eighty-four thousand five hundred households.

literal: On the throne thirteen years he died; temple name Renzong.
idiomatic: On the throne thirteen years he died; temple name Renzong.

literal: Yilie's sister Pusuwan
idiomatic: Yilie's sister Pusuwan

literal: The son was young; testamentary edict had younger sister Pusuwan hold state; she held rule, changed the era to Chongfu, title Chengtian Empress Dowager.
idiomatic: The son was young; testamentary edict had younger sister Pusuwan hold state; she held rule, changed the era to Chongfu, title Chengtian Empress Dowager.

literal: Later she had relations with the consort's younger brother Puguzhi Shali; she sent the consort out as Prince of Dongping and on false charges killed him.
idiomatic: Later she had relations with the consort's younger brother Puguzhi Shali; she sent the consort out as Prince of Dongping and on false charges killed him.

literal: The consort's father Wolila led troops surrounding her palace and shot Pusuwan and Puguzhi Shali to death.
idiomatic: The consort's father Wolila led troops surrounding her palace and shot Pusuwan and Puguzhi Shali to death.

literal: Pusuwan was on the throne fourteen years.
idiomatic: Pusuwan was on the throne fourteen years.

literal: Yilie's second son Zhilugu
idiomatic: Yilie's second son Zhilugu

literal: 【Commentary and Appraisal】
idiomatic: 【Commentary and Appraisal】

literal: Yelü Chun in Tianzuo's age twice ruled the great state, received the gold warrant, was praised in bowing and not called by name.
idiomatic: In Tianzuo's reign Yelü Chun twice ruled the great state, received the gold warrant, and was honored with bowing while not called by name.

literal: For a time his favor had no equal.
idiomatic: For a time no favor could compare with his.

literal: When Tianzuo was driven from his capital, as commander-in-chief guarding Nanjing, could he alone not rouse great righteousness to stir the Yan people and the great ministers, raise troops loyal to the throne, resist Jin in the east and welcome Tianzuo?
idiomatic: When Tianzuo was driven from his capital, could he not—as commander-in-chief at Nanjing—have roused great righteousness among the Yan people and great ministers, raised a loyal host to resist Jin in the east, and welcomed Tianzuo home?

literal: Yet he took it for himself — that was usurpation.
idiomatic: Yet he seized the throne for himself—that was usurpation.

literal: How much more did he bear Tianzuo!
idiomatic: And how he wronged Tianzuo!

literal: Dashi had made Chun emperor yet still served Tianzuo; he returned to Tianzuo.
idiomatic: Dashi had made Chun emperor, yet still served Tianzuo when he returned.

literal: Tianzuo blamed him with great righteousness; he thereupon styled himself king and left.
idiomatic: Tianzuo rebuked him on grounds of righteousness; Dashi thereupon styled himself king and departed.

literal: Fortunately relying on the ancestors' remaining might and lingering wisdom, he established a title ten thousand li away.
idiomatic: By fortune of the ancestors' remaining might and lingering wisdom, he established a realm ten thousand li away.

literal: Though a widowed mother and weak son succeeded one another in turn, for nearly ninety years — one may also call that difficult.
idiomatic: Though a widowed mother and weak son handed on rule in turn for nearly ninety years, one may still call that an achievement hard-won.

literal: Yet Chun's, Yali's, and Dashi's establishments were all in Tianzuo's age.
idiomatic: Yet the enthronements of Chun, Yali, and Dashi all fell within Tianzuo's lifetime.

literal: Having a lord yet making another lord — can that be permitted?
idiomatic: To have a sovereign yet set up another—how can that be permitted?

literal: When Zhuge the Martial Marquis held mourning for Emperor Xian and afterward set up the Former Lord as emperor — that cannot be spoken of in the same year.
idiomatic: When Zhuge the Martial Marquis mourned Emperor Xian and afterward enthroned the Former Lord—that is not a case to be named in the same breath.

literal: Therefore it is set forth as a warning.
idiomatic: Therefore this is recorded as a warning.

literal: Appraisal: Liao rose from the northern wilds; the flourishing of arms and armor — drums marched beyond the frontier, swept Hebei, planted Jin and set up Han — how magnificent!
idiomatic: Appraisal: Liao rose from the northern wilds; arms and armor flourished—drums marched beyond the frontier, swept Hebei, planted Jin and raised Han—how magnificent!

literal: Taizu and Taizong rode the momentum of a hundred battles, gathered a newly made state — heroic stratagem and design may be called far-reaching.
idiomatic: Taizu and Taizong rode the momentum of a hundred battles and gathered a newly forged state; their heroic stratagem and design may be called far-sighted indeed.

literal: Though Shizong was middling talent and Muzong cruel and violent, successive misfortunes of regicide and treason came — yet the sacred vessel did not shake.
idiomatic: Though Shizong was middling in talent and Muzong cruel and violent, regicide and treason followed in succession—yet the sacred vessel did not tremble.

literal: Surely because the ancestors' awesomeness and orders still sufficed to shake and fold their own people.
idiomatic: Surely because the ancestors' awesomeness and commands still sufficed to overawe their own people.

literal: From Shengzong onward they cultivated government within and extended territory without.
idiomatic: From Shengzong onward they cultivated government within and extended territory without.

literal: Thereafter they renewed solid neighborly goodwill; the four borders were secure.
idiomatic: Thereafter they renewed firm neighborly goodwill, and the four borders were secure.

literal: Maintaining a foundation of more than two hundred years had its reasons.
idiomatic: That a foundation of more than two hundred years was maintained had its reasons.

literal: Descending to Tianzuo, he both met the final fate and disappointed human expectation, trusted wicked flatterers, himself undermined the state's root — the masses below lost heart.
idiomatic: Descending to Tianzuo, he met the dynasty's final fate and disappointed the people's hopes, trusted wicked flatterers, and himself undermined the state's root—those below lost heart.

literal: When Jin troops gathered, internal trouble arose first; plots to depose and enthrone, traces of rebellion and flight, followed one another like bees.
idiomatic: When Jin troops gathered, internal trouble arose first; plots to depose and enthrone and trails of rebellion and flight swarmed like bees.

literal: Leading to earth collapsing and tiles disintegrating, beyond recovery — truly pitiable!
idiomatic: The realm collapsed like earth and tiles beyond recovery—truly pitiable!

literal: Yelü and Xiao for generations were nephew and uncle; righteousness was the same as shared weal and woe.
idiomatic: Yelü and Xiao for generations were nephew and uncle; their bond was shared weal and woe.

literal: Fengxian took private interest and destroyed the public good, first caused disaster and raised difficulty, until it reached this.
idiomatic: Fengxian put private interest above the public good, first stirred disaster and difficulty, until matters came to this pass.

literal: Tianzuo in extremity at last understood Fengxian had misled him — was it not nearly too late?
idiomatic: Tianzuo in extremity at last saw that Fengxian had misled him—was it not nearly too late?

literal: Chun and Yali are what is called: the name not correct, speech not in accord, the affair not accomplished.
idiomatic: Of Chun and Yali it is said: when the name is not correct, speech does not accord, and the affair is not accomplished.

literal: Dashi barely prolonged — he was better at this; yet how many years more?
idiomatic: Dashi barely prolonged the line—better than the others, yet for how many years more?

literal: Collation Notes
idiomatic: Collation Notes

literal: 1: "Reached Tiande" — According to Jin History 82 Xiao Zhonggong's biography reads "reached Huolidipo."
idiomatic: 1: "Reached Tiande" — According to Jin History 82 Xiao Zhonggong's biography reads "reached Huolidipo."

literal: 2: "In early Qingning the Empress Dowager raised him" — Chun died in Baoda year 2; if "age sixty" is correct he would have been born in Qingning year 9; "early Qingning" has a textual error.
idiomatic: 2: "In early Qingning the Empress Dowager raised him" — Chun died in Baoda year 2; if "age sixty" is correct he would have been born in Qingning year 9; "early Qingning" has a textual error.

literal: 3: "When Tianzuo took the throne, advanced Prince of Zheng" — According to the annals, in the sixth month of Qianyun year 1 Northern Ping Commandery King Chun was advanced Prince of Zheng.
idiomatic: 3: "When Tianzuo took the throne, advanced Prince of Zheng" — According to the annals, in the sixth month of Qianyun year 1 Northern Ping Commandery King Chun was advanced Prince of Zheng.

literal: 4: "Qianyun year 2, advanced Prince of Yue" — According to the annals, in the eleventh month of Qianyun year 3 Prince of Zheng Chun was advanced King of Yue.
idiomatic: 4: "Qianyun year 2, advanced Prince of Yue" — According to the annals, in the eleventh month of Qianyun year 3 Prince of Zheng Chun was advanced King of Yue.

literal: 5: Chancellor Li Chun — According to the annals Baoda year 2 third month and juan 102 his biography all read Li Chuwenn.
idiomatic: 5: Chancellor Li Chun — According to the annals Baoda year 2 third month and juan 102 his biography all read Li Chuwenn.

literal: 6: Great Yellow Shivewei and eighteen tribes — Dila: Offices Annals 2 reads Dilie;
idiomatic: 6: Great Yellow Shivewei and eighteen tribes — Dila: Offices Annals 2 reads Dilie;

literal: Wangjila is Jin History's Guangjici and Yuan History's Hongjila;
idiomatic: Wangjila is Jin History's Guangjici and Yuan History's Hongjila;

literal: Chachila: annals Da'an year 10 fourth month and Offices Annals 2 both read Chazhala, which is Yuan History's Zhazhalaite;
idiomatic: Chachila: annals Da'an year 10 fourth month and Offices Annals 2 both read Chazhala, which is Yuan History's Zhazhalaite;

literal: Bigude: Offices Annals 2 reads Biguode;
idiomatic: Bigude: Offices Annals 2 reads Biguode;

literal: Mierji: annals Shoulong year 3 second month reads Meiliji, which is Yuan Secret History's Mierqi;
idiomatic: Mierji: annals Shoulong year 3 second month reads Meiliji, which is Yuan Secret History's Mierqi;

literal: Humusi is Offices Annals 2's Humusi Mountain Tribe, Military Guard Annals lower's Humusi Mountain fan;
idiomatic: Humusi is Offices Annals 2's Humusi Mountain Tribe, Military Guard Annals lower's Humusi Mountain fan;

literal: Jiuerbi: Tribal Relations table reads Jierbi.
idiomatic: Jiuerbi: Tribal Relations table reads Jierbi.

literal: 7: Buguhan city — Luo collation says it is the Old Uighur city in Taizu Annals.
idiomatic: 7: Buguhan city — Luo collation says it is the Old Uighur city in Taizu Annals.

literal: 8: Xiao Chala Abu — Below reads Xiao Zhala Abu.
idiomatic: 8: Xiao Chala Abu — Below reads Xiao Zhala Abu.
